quotes.text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, perish like old herons in a lake without fish.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, lie, like broken bows, sighing after the past.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others; thus a wise man will not suffer.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man make himself as he teaches others to be, then, being himself well subdued, he may subdue (others); one's own self is indeed difficult to subdue.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The virtuous man delights in this world, and he delights in the next; he delights in both. He delights and rejoices, when he sees the purity of his own work.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The evil done by oneself, self-begotten, self-bred, crushes the foolish, as a diamond breaks a precious stone.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whose wickedness is very great brings himself down to that state where his enemy wishes him to be, as a creeper does with the tree which it surrounds.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Bad deeds, and deeds hurtful to ourselves, are easy to do; what is beneficial and good, that is very difficult to do.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The foolish man who scorns the rule of the venerable (Arahat), of the elect (Ariya), of the virtuous, and follows false doctrine, he bears fruit to his own destruction, like the fruits of the Katthaka reed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let no one forget his own duty for the sake of another's, however great; let a man, after he has discerned his own duty, be always attentive to his duty.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Do not follow the evil law! Do not live on in thoughtlessness! Do not follow false doctrine! Be not a friend of the world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Rouse thyself! do not be idle! Follow the law of virtue! The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Follow the law of virtue; do not follow that of sin. The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The evil-doer suffers in this world, and he suffers in the next; he suffers in both. He suffers when he thinks of the evil he has done; he suffers more when going on the evil path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Look upon the world as a bubble, look upon it as a mirage: the king of death does not see him who thus looks down upon the world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Come, look at this glittering world, like unto a royal chariot; the foolish are immersed in it, but the wise do not touch it.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who formerly was reckless and afterwards became sober, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whose evil deeds are covered by good deeds, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: This world is dark, few only can see here; a few only go to heaven, like birds escaped from the net.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The swans go on the path of the sun, they go through the ether by means of their miraculous power; the wise are led out of this world, when they have conquered Mara and his train.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man has transgressed one law, and speaks lies, and scoffs at another world, there is no evil he will not do.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The uncharitable do not go to the world of the gods; fools only do not praise liberality; a wise man rejoices in liberality, and through it becomes blessed in the other world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Better than sovereignty over the earth, better than going to heaven, better than lordship over all worlds, is the reward of the first step in holiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whose conquest is not conquered again, into whose conquest no one in this world enters, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The virtuous man is happy in this world, and he is happy in the next; he is happy in both. He is happy when he thinks of the good he has done; he is still more happy when going on the good path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whom no desire with its snares and poisons can lead astray, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Even the gods envy those who are awakened and not forgetful, who are given to meditation, who are wise, and who delight in the repose of retirement (from the world).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Difficult (to obtain) is the conception of men, difficult is the life of mortals, difficult is the hearing of the True Law, difficult is the birth of the Awakened (the attainment of Buddhahood).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The Awakened call patience the highest penance, long-suffering the highest Nirvana; for he is not an anchorite (pravragita) who strikes others, he is not an ascetic (sramana) who insults others.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not to blame, not to strike, to live restrained under the law, to be moderate in eating, to sleep and sit alone, and to dwell on the highest thoughts,--this is the teaching of the Awakened.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no satisfying lusts, even by a shower of gold pieces; he who knows that lusts have a short taste and cause pain, he is wise;
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Even in heavenly pleasures he finds no satisfaction, the disciple who is fully awakened delights only in the destruction of all desires.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Men, driven by fear, go to many a refuge, to mountains and forests, to groves and sacred trees.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But that is not a safe refuge, that is not the best refuge; a man is not delivered from all pains after having gone to that refuge.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The thoughtless man, even if he can recite a large portion (of the law), but is not a doer of it, has no share in the priesthood, but is like a cowherd counting the cows of others.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who takes refuge with Buddha, the Law, and the Church; he who, with clear understanding, sees the four holy truths:--
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Viz. pain, the origin of pain, the destruction of pain, and the eightfold holy way that leads to the quieting of pain;--
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: That is the safe refuge, that is the best refuge; having gone to that refuge, a man is delivered from all pain.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A supernatural person (a Buddha) is not easily found, he is not born everywhere. Wherever such a sage is born, that race prospers.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who pays homage to those who deserve homage, whether the awakened (Buddha) or their disciples, those who have overcome the host (of evils), and crossed the flood of sorrow, he who pays homage to such as have found deliverance and know no fear, his merit can never be measured by anybody.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let us live happily then, free from ailments among the ailing! among men who are ailing let us dwell free from ailments!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let us live happily then, free from greed among the greedy! among men who are greedy let us dwell free from greed!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The follower of the law, even if he can recite only a small portion (of the law), but, having forsaken passion and hatred and foolishness, possesses true knowledge and serenity of mind, he, caring for nothing in this world or that to come, has indeed a share in the priesthood.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let us live happily then, though we call nothing our own! We shall be like the bright gods, feeding on happiness!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Victory breeds hatred, for the conquered is unhappy. He who has given up both victory and defeat, he, the contented, is happy.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no fire like passion; there is no losing throw like hatred; there is no pain like this body; there is no happiness higher than rest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Hunger is the worst of diseases, the body the greatest of pains; if one knows this truly, that is Nirvana, the highest happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentedness the best riches; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who has tasted the sweetness of solitude and tranquillity, is free from fear and free from sin, while he tastes the sweetness of drinking in the law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The sight of the elect (Arya) is good, to live with them is always happiness; if a man does not see fools, he will be truly happy.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who walks in the company of fools suffers a long way; company with fools, as with an enemy, is always painful; company with the wise is pleasure, like meeting with kinsfolk.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Therefore, one ought to follow the wise, the intelligent, the learned, the much enduring, the dutiful, the elect; one ought to follow a good and wise man, as the moon follows the path of the stars.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who gives himself to vanity, and does not give himself to meditation, forgetting the real aim (of life) and grasping at pleasure, will in time envy him who has exerted himself in meditation.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Earnestness is the path of immortality (Nirvana), thoughtlessness the path of death. Those who are in earnest do not die, those who are thoughtless are as if dead already.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let no man ever look for what is pleasant, or what is unpleasant. Not to see what is pleasant is pain, and it is pain to see what is unpleasant.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let, therefore, no man love anything; loss of the beloved is evil. Those who love nothing and hate nothing, have no fetters.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: From pleasure comes grief, from pleasure comes fear; he who is free from pleasure knows neither grief nor fear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: From affection comes grief, from affection comes fear; he who is free from affection knows neither grief nor fear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: From lust comes grief, from lust comes fear; he who is free from lust knows neither grief nor fear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: From love comes grief, from love comes fear; he who is free from love knows neither grief nor fear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: From greed comes grief, from greed comes fear; he who is free from greed knows neither grief nor fear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who possesses virtue and intelligence, who is just, speaks the truth, and does what is his own business, him the world will hold dear.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He in whom a desire for the Ineffable (Nirvana) has sprung up, who is satisfied in his mind, and whose thoughts are not bewildered by love, he is called urdhvamsrotas (carried upwards by the stream).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Kinsmen, friends, and lovers salute a man who has been long away, and returns safe from afar.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Those who are advanced in earnestness, having understood this clearly, delight in earnestness, and rejoice in the knowledge of the Ariyas (the elect).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: In like manner his good works receive him who has done good, and has gone from this world to the other;--as kinsmen receive a friend on his return.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let a man leave anger, let him forsake pride, let him overcome all bondage! No sufferings befall the man who is not attached to name and form, and who calls nothing his own.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who holds back rising anger like a rolling chariot, him I call a real driver; other people are but holding the reins.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Speak the truth, do not yield to anger; give, if thou art asked for little; by these three steps thou wilt go near the gods.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The sages who injure nobody, and who always control their body, they will go to the unchangeable place (Nirvana), where, if they have gone, they will suffer no more.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Those who are ever watchful, who study day and night, and who strive after Nirvana, their passions will come to an end.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: This is an old saying, O Atula, this is not only of to-day: `They blame him who sits silent, they blame him who speaks much, they also blame him who says little; there is no one on earth who is not blamed.'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There never was, there never will be, nor is there now, a man who is always blamed, or a man who is always praised.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But he whom those who discriminate praise continually day after day, as without blemish, wise, rich in knowledge and virtue, who would dare to blame him, like a coin made of gold from the Gambu river? Even the gods praise him, he is praised even by Brahman.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: These wise people, meditative, steady, always possessed of strong powers, attain to Nirvana, the highest happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Beware of bodily anger, and control thy body! Leave the sins of the body, and with thy body practise virtue!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Beware of the anger of the tongue, and control thy tongue! Leave the sins of the tongue, and practise virtue with thy tongue!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Beware of the anger of the mind, and control thy mind! Leave the sins of the mind, and practise virtue with thy mind!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The wise who control their body, who control their tongue, the wise who control their mind, are indeed well controlled.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Thou art now like a sear leaf, the messengers of death (Yama) have come near to thee; thou standest at the door of thy departure, and thou hast no provision for thy journey.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise! When thy impurities are blown away, and thou art free from guilt, thou wilt enter into the heavenly world of the elect (Ariya).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Thy life has come to an end, thou art come near to death (Yama), there is no resting-place for thee on the road, and thou hast no provision for thy journey.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise! When thy impurities are blown away, and thou art free from guilt, thou wilt not enter again into birth and decay.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let a wise man blow off the impurities of his self, as a smith blows off the impurities of silver one by one, little by little, and from time to time.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If an earnest person has roused himself, if he is not forgetful, if his deeds are pure, if he acts with consideration, if he restrains himself, and lives according to law,--then his glory will increase.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As the impurity which springs from the iron, when it springs from it, destroys it; thus do a transgressor's own works lead him to the evil path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The taint of prayers is non-repetition; the taint of houses, non-repair; the taint of the body is sloth; the taint of a watchman, thoughtlessness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Bad conduct is the taint of woman, greediness the taint of a benefactor; tainted are all evil ways in this world and in the next.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But there is a taint worse than all taints,--ignorance is the greatest taint. O mendicants! throw off that taint, and become taintless!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Life is easy to live for a man who is without shame, a crow hero, a mischief-maker, an insulting, bold, and wretched fellow.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But life is hard to live for a modest man, who always looks for what is pure, who is disinterested, quiet, spotless, and intelligent.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who destroys life, who speaks untruth, who in this world takes what is not given him, who goes to another man's wife;
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: And the man who gives himself to drinking intoxicating liquors, he, even in this world, digs up his own root.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: O man, know this, that the unrestrained are in a bad state; take care that greediness and vice do not bring thee to grief for a long time!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The world gives according to their faith or according to their pleasure: if a man frets about the food and the drink given to others, he will find no rest either by day or by night.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He in whom that feeling is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, finds rest by day and by night.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no fire like passion, there is no shark like hatred, there is no snare like folly, there is no torrent like greed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fault of others is easily perceived, but that of oneself is difficult to perceive; a man winnows his neighbour's faults like chaff, but his own fault he hides, as a cheat hides the bad die from the gambler.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man looks after the faults of others, and is always inclined to be offended, his own passions will grow, and he is far from the destruction of passions.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. The world delights in vanity, the Tathagatas (the Buddhas) are free from vanity.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. No creatures are eternal; but the awakened (Buddha) are never shaken.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not just if he carries a matter by violence; no, he who distinguishes both right and wrong, who is learned and leads others, not by violence, but by law and equity, and who is guarded by the law and intelligent, he is called just.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not a supporter of the law because he talks much; even if a man has learnt little, but sees the law bodily, he is a supporter of the law, a man who never neglects the law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Fools follow after vanity, men of evil wisdom. The wise man keeps earnestness as his best jewel.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not an elder because his head is grey; his age may be ripe, but he is called `Old-in-vain.'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He in whom there is truth, virtue, love, restraint, moderation, he who is free from impurity and is wise, he is called an elder.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: An envious greedy, dishonest man does not become respectable by means of much talking only, or by the beauty of his complexion.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He in whom all this is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, he, when freed from hatred and wise, is called respectable.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not by tonsure does an undisciplined man who speaks falsehood become a Samana; can a man be a Samana who is still held captive by desire and greediness?
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who always quiets the evil, whether small or large, he is called a Samana (a quiet man), because he has quieted all evil.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not a mendicant (Bhikshu) simply because he asks others for alms; he who adopts the whole law is a Bhikshu, not he who only begs.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who is above good and evil, who is chaste, who with knowledge passes through the world, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not a Muni because he observes silence (mona, i.e. mauna), if he is foolish and ignorant; but the wise who, taking the balance, chooses the good and avoids evil, he is a Muni, and is a Muni thereby; he who in this world weighs both sides is called a Muni.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Follow not after vanity, nor after the enjoyment of love and lust! He who is earnest and meditative, obtains ample joy.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man is not an elect (Ariya) because he injures living creatures; because he has pity on all living creatures, therefore is a man called Ariya.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not only by discipline and vows, not only by much learning, not by entering into a trance, not by sleeping alone, do I earn the happiness of release which no worldling can know. Bhikshu, be not confident as long as thou hast not attained the extinction of desires.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The best of ways is the eightfold; the best of truths the four words; the best of virtues passionlessness; the best of men he who has eyes to see.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: This is the way, there is no other that leads to the purifying of intelligence. Go on this way! Everything else is the deceit of Mara (the tempter).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If you go on this way, you will make an end of pain! The way was preached by me, when I had understood the removal of the thorns (in the flesh).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: `All created things perish,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way to purity.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: `All created things are grief and pain,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: `All forms are unreal,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: When the learned man drives away vanity by earnestness, he, the wise, climbing the terraced heights of wisdom, looks down upon the fools, serene he looks upon the toiling crowd, as one that stands on a mountain looks down upon them that stand upon the plain.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who does not rouse himself when it is time to rise, who, though young and strong, is full of sloth, whose will and thought are weak, that lazy and idle man will never find the way to knowledge.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Watching his speech, well restrained in mind, let a man never commit any wrong with his body! Let a man but keep these three roads of action clear, and he will achieve the way which is taught by the wise.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Through zeal knowledge is gotten, through lack of zeal knowledge is lost; let a man who knows this double path of gain and loss thus place himself that knowledge may grow.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Cut down the whole forest (of lust), not a tree only! Danger comes out of the forest (of lust). When you have cut down both the forest (of lust) and its undergrowth, then, Bhikshus, you will be rid of the forest and free!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: So long as the love of man towards women, even the smallest, is not destroyed, so long is his mind in bondage, as the calf that drinks milk is to its mother.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Cut out the love of self, like an autumn lotus, with thy hand! Cherish the road of peace. Nirvana has been shown by Sugata (Buddha).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: `Here I shall dwell in the rain, here in winter and summer,' thus the fool meditates, and does not think of his death.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Death comes and carries off that man, praised for his children and flocks, his mind distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Sons are no help, nor a father, nor relations; there is no help from kinsfolk for one whom death has seized.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A wise and good man who knows the meaning of this, should quickly clear the way that leads to Nirvana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Earnest among the thoughtless, awake among the sleepers, the wise man advances like a racer, leaving behind the hack.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If by leaving a small pleasure one sees a great pleasure, let a wise man leave the small pleasure, and look to the great.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who, by causing pain to others, wishes to obtain pleasure for himself, he, entangled in the bonds of hatred, will never be free from hatred.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: What ought to be done is neglected, what ought not to be done is done; the desires of unruly, thoughtless people are always increasing.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But they whose whole watchfulness is always directed to their body, who do not follow what ought not to be done, and who steadfastly do what ought to be done, the desires of such watchful and wise people will come to an end.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two valiant kings, though he has destroyed a kingdom with all its subjects.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two holy kings, and an eminent man besides.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama (Buddha) are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on Buddha.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the church.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on their body.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who harbour such thoughts hatred will never cease.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: By earnestness did Maghavan (Indra) rise to the lordship of the gods. People praise earnestness; thoughtlessness is always blamed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in meditation.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Whatever place a faithful, virtuous, celebrated, and wealthy man chooses, there he is respected.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He alone who, without ceasing, practises the duty of sitting alone and sleeping alone, he, subduing himself, will rejoice in the destruction of all desires alone, as if living in a forest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who says what is not, goes to hell; he also who, having done a thing, says I have not done it. After death both are equal, they are men with evil deeds in the next world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Many men whose shoulders are covered with the yellow gown are ill-conditioned and unrestrained; such evil-doers by their evil deeds go to hell.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Better it would be to swallow a heated iron ball, like flaring fire, than that a bad unrestrained fellow should live on the charity of the land.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Four things does a wreckless man gain who covets his neighbour's wife,--a bad reputation, an uncomfortable bed, thirdly, punishment, and lastly, hell.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in earnestness, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, moves about like fire, burning all his fetters, small or large.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is bad reputation, and the evil way (to hell), there is the short pleasure of the frightened in the arms of the frightened, and the king imposes heavy punishment; therefore let no man think of his neighbour's wife.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As a grass-blade, if badly grasped, cuts the arm, badly-practised asceticism leads to hell.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: An act carelessly performed, a broken vow, and hesitating obedience to discipline, all this brings no great reward.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If anything is to be done, let a man do it, let him attack it vigorously! A careless pilgrim only scatters the dust of his passions more widely.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Like a well-guarded frontier fort, with defences within and without, so let a man guard himself. Not a moment should escape, for they who allow the right moment to pass, suffer pain when they are in hell.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They who are ashamed of what they ought not to be ashamed of, and are not ashamed of what they ought to be ashamed of, such men, embracing false doctrines enter the evil path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They who fear when they ought not to fear, and fear not when they ought to fear, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They who forbid when there is nothing to be forbidden, and forbid not when there is something to be forbidden, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in reflection, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, cannot fall away (from his perfect state)--he is close upon Nirvana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Silently shall I endure abuse as the elephant in battle endures the arrow sent from the bow: for the world is ill-natured.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They lead a tamed elephant to battle, the king mounts a tamed elephant; the tamed is the best among men, he who silently endures abuse.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: For with these animals does no man reach the untrodden country (Nirvana), where a tamed man goes on a tamed animal, viz. on his own well-tamed self.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The elephant called Dhanapalaka, his temples running with sap, and difficult to hold, does not eat a morsel when bound; the elephant longs for the elephant grove.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man becomes fat and a great eater, if he is sleepy and rolls himself about, that fool, like a hog fed on wash, is born again and again.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: This mind of mine went formerly wandering about as it liked, as it listed, as it pleased; but I shall now hold it in thoroughly, as the rider who holds the hook holds in the furious elephant.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Be not thoughtless, watch your thoughts! Draw yourself out of the evil way, like an elephant sunk in mud.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man find a prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, he may walk with him, overcoming all dangers, happy, but considerate.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man find no prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, let him walk alone, like a king who has left his conquered country behind,--like an elephant in the forest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought, which is difficult to guard, difficult to hold back.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: It is better to live alone, there is no companionship with a fool; let a man walk alone, let him commit no sin, with few wishes, like an elephant in the forest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If an occasion arises, friends are pleasant; enjoyment is pleasant, whatever be the cause; a good work is pleasant in the hour of death; the giving up of all grief is pleasant.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Pleasant in the world is the state of a mother, pleasant the state of a father, pleasant the state of a Samana, pleasant the state of a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Pleasant is virtue lasting to old age, pleasant is a faith firmly rooted; pleasant is attainment of intelligence, pleasant is avoiding of sins.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The thirst of a thoughtless man grows like a creeper; he runs from life to life, like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Whomsoever this fierce thirst overcomes, full of poison, in this world, his sufferings increase like the abounding Birana grass.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who overcomes this fierce thirst, difficult to be conquered in this world, sufferings fall off from him, like water-drops from a lotus leaf.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: This salutary word I tell you, `Do ye, as many as are here assembled, dig up the root of thirst, as he who wants the sweet-scented Usira root must dig up the Birana grass, that Mara (the tempter) may not crush you again and again, as the stream crushes the reeds.'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As a tree, even though it has been cut down, is firm so long as its root is safe, and grows again, thus, unless the feeders of thirst are destroyed, the pain (of life) will return again and again.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whose thirst running towards pleasure is exceeding strong in the thirty-six channels, the waves will carry away that misguided man, viz. his desires which are set on passion.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As a fish taken from his watery home and thrown on dry ground, our thought trembles all over in order to escape the dominion of Mara (the tempter).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The channels run everywhere, the creeper (of passion) stands sprouting; if you see the creeper springing up, cut its root by means of knowledge.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A creature's pleasures are extravagant and luxurious; sunk in lust and looking for pleasure, men undergo (again and again) birth and decay.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; held in fetters and bonds, they undergo pain for a long time, again and again.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; let therefore the mendicant drive out thirst, by striving after passionlessness for himself.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who having got rid of the forest (of lust) (i.e. after having reached Nirvana) gives himself over to forest-life (i.e. to lust), and who, when removed from the forest (i.e. from lust), runs to the forest (i.e. to lust), look at that man! though free, he runs into bondage.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Wise people do not call that a strong fetter which is made of iron, wood, or hemp; far stronger is the care for precious stones and rings, for sons and a wife.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: That fetter wise people call strong which drags down, yields, but is difficult to undo; after having cut this at last, people leave the world, free from cares, and leaving desires and pleasures behind.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Those who are slaves to passions, run down with the stream (of desires), as a spider runs down the web which he has made himself; when they have cut this, at last, wise people leave the world free from cares, leaving all affection behind.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Give up what is before, give up what is behind, give up what is in the middle, when thou goest to the other shore of existence; if thy mind is altogether free, thou wilt not again enter into birth and decay.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man is tossed about by doubts, full of strong passions, and yearning only for what is delightful, his thirst will grow more and more, and he will indeed make his fetters strong.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man delights in quieting doubts, and, always reflecting, dwells on what is not delightful (the impurity of the body, &c.), he certainly will remove, nay, he will cut the fetter of Mara.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who has reached the consummation, who does not tremble, who is without thirst and without sin, he has broken all the thorns of life: this will be his last body.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who is without thirst and without affection, who understands the words and their interpretation, who knows the order of letters (those which are before and which are after), he has received his last body, he is called the great sage, the great man.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: `I have conquered all, I know all, in all conditions of life I am free from taint; I have left all, and through the destruction of thirst I am free; having learnt myself, whom shall I teach?'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The gift of the law exceeds all gifts; the sweetness of the law exceeds all sweetness; the delight in the law exceeds all delights; the extinction of thirst overcomes all pain.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Pleasures destroy the foolish, if they look not for the other shore; the foolish by his thirst for pleasures destroys himself, as if he were his own enemy.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by passion: therefore a gift bestowed on the passionless brings great reward.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by vanity: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from vanity brings great reward.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by lust: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from lust brings great reward.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who controls his hand, he who controls his feet, he who controls his speech, he who is well controlled, he who delights inwardly, who is collected, who is solitary and content, him they call Bhikshu.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The Bhikshu who controls his mouth, who speaks wisely and calmly, who teaches the meaning and the law, his word is sweet.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who dwells in the law, delights in the law, meditates on the law, follows the law, that Bhikshu will never fall away from the true law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let him not despise what he has received, nor ever envy others: a mendicant who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A Bhikshu who, though he receives little, does not despise what he has received, even the gods will praise him, if his life is pure, and if he is not slothful.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who never identifies himself with name and form, and does not grieve over what is no more, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: O Bhikshu, empty this boat! if emptied, it will go quickly; having cut off passion and hatred thou wilt go to Nirvana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Those who bridle their mind which travels far, moves about alone, is without a body, and hides in the chamber (of the heart), will be free from the bonds of Mara (the tempter).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Cut off the five (senses), leave the five, rise above the five. A Bhikshu, who has escaped from the five fetters, he is called Oghatinna, `saved from the flood.'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Meditate, O Bhikshu, and be not heedless! Do not direct thy thought to what gives pleasure that thou mayest not for thy heedlessness have to swallow the iron ball (in hell), and that thou mayest not cry out when burning, `This is pain.'
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A Bhikshu who has entered his empty house, and whose mind is tranquil, feels a more than human delight when he sees the law clearly.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As soon as he has considered the origin and destruction of the elements (khandha) of the body, he finds happiness and joy which belong to those who know the immortal (Nirvana).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: And this is the beginning here for a wise Bhikshu: watchfulness over the senses, contentedness, restraint under the law; keep noble friends whose life is pure, and who are not slothful.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let him live in charity, let him be perfect in his duties; then in the fulness of delight he will make an end of suffering.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As the Vassika plant sheds its withered flowers, men should shed passion and hatred, O ye Bhikshus!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The Bhikshu whose body and tongue and mind are quieted, who is collected, and has rejected the baits of the world, he is called quiet.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man's thoughts are unsteady, if he does not know the true law, if his peace of mind is troubled, his knowledge will never be perfect.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: For self is the lord of self, self is the refuge of self; therefore curb thyself as the merchant curbs a good horse.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The Bhikshu, full of delight, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who, even as a young Bhikshu, applies himself to the doctrine of Buddha, brightens up this world, like the moon when free from clouds.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Stop the stream valiantly, drive away the desires, O Brahmana! When you have understood the destruction of all that was made, you will understand that which was not made.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If the Brahmana has reached the other shore in both laws (in restraint and contemplation), all bonds vanish from him who has obtained knowledge.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He for whom there is neither this nor that shore, nor both, him, the fearless and unshackled, I call indeed a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who is thoughtful, blameless, settled, dutiful, without passions, and who has attained the highest end, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The sun is bright by day, the moon shines by night, the warrior is bright in his armour, the Brahmana is bright in his meditation; but Buddha, the Awakened, is bright with splendour day and night.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Because a man is rid of evil, therefore he is called Brahmana; because he walks quietly, therefore he is called Samana; because he has sent away his own impurities, therefore he is called Pravragita (Pabbagita, a pilgrim).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: No one should attack a Brahmana, but no Brahmana (if attacked) should let himself fly at his aggressor! Woe to him who strikes a Brahmana, more woe to him who flies at his aggressor!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a man's thoughts are not dissipated, if his mind is not perplexed, if he has ceased to think of good or evil, then there is no fear for him while he is watchful.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: It advantages a Brahmana not a little if he holds his mind back from the pleasures of life; when all wish to injure has vanished, pain will cease.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: After a man has once understood the law as taught by the Well-awakened (Buddha), let him worship it carefully, as the Brahmana worships the sacrificial fire.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: A man does not become a Brahmana by his platted hair, by his family, or by birth; in whom there is truth and righteousness, he is blessed, he is a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: What is the use of platted hair, O fool! what of the raiment of goat-skins? Within thee there is ravening, but the outside thou makest clean.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The man who wears dirty raiments, who is emaciated and covered with veins, who lives alone in the forest, and meditates, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: I do not call a man a Brahmana because of his origin or of his mother. He is indeed arrogant, and he is wealthy: but the poor, who is free from all attachments, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut all fetters, who never trembles, is independent and unshackled.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut the strap and the thong, the chain with all that pertains to it, who has burst the bar, and is awakened.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, though he has committed no offence, endures reproach, bonds, and stripes, who has endurance for his force, and strength for his army.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who do not harbour such thoughts hatred will cease.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Knowing that this body is (fragile) like a jar, and making this thought firm like a fortress, one should attack Mara (the tempter) with the weapon of knowledge, one should watch him when conquered, and should never rest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is free from anger, dutiful, virtuous, without appetite, who is subdued, and has received his last body.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not cling to pleasures, like water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on the point of a needle.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, even here, knows the end of his suffering, has put down his burden, and is unshackled.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose knowledge is deep, who possesses wisdom, who knows the right way and the wrong, and has attained the highest end.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who keeps aloof both from laymen and from mendicants, who frequents no houses, and has but few desires.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who finds no fault with other beings, whether feeble or strong, and does not kill nor cause slaughter.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is tolerant with the intolerant, mild with fault-finders, and free from passion among the passionate.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana from whom anger and hatred, pride and envy have dropt like a mustard seed from the point of a needle.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who takes nothing in the world that is not given him, be it long or short, small or large, good or bad.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Before long, alas! this body will lie on the earth, despised, without understanding, like a useless log.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who fosters no desires for this world or for the next, has no inclinations, and is unshackled.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has no interests, and when he has understood (the truth), does not say How, how? and who has reached the depth of the Immortal.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world is above good and evil, above the bondage of both, free from grief from sin, and from impurity.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is bright like the moon, pure, serene, undisturbed, and in whom all gaiety is extinct.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has traversed this miry road, the impassable world and its vanity, who has gone through, and reached the other shore, is thoughtful, guileless, free from doubts, free from attachment, and content.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy, a wrongly-directed mind will do us greater mischief.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Who shall overcome this earth, and the world of Yama (the lord of the departed), and the world of the gods? Who shall find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower?
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The disciple will overcome the earth, and the world of Yama, and the world of the gods. The disciple will find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who knows that this body is like froth, and has learnt that it is as unsubstantial as a mirage, will break the flower-pointed arrow of Mara, and never see the king of death.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Death carries off a man who is gathering flowers and whose mind is distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Death subdues a man who is gathering flowers, and whose mind is distracted, before he is satiated in his pleasures.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Like a beautiful flower, full of colour, but without scent, are the fine but fruitless words of him who does not act accordingly.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But, like a beautiful flower, full of colour and full of scent, are the fine and fruitful words of him who acts accordingly.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As many kinds of wreaths can be made from a heap of flowers, so many good things may be achieved by a mortal when once he is born.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Mean is the scent that comes from Tagara and sandal-wood;--the perfume of those who possess virtue rises up to the gods as the highest.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Of the people who possess these virtues, who live without thoughtlessness, and who are emancipated through true knowledge, Mara, the tempter, never finds the way.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As on a heap of rubbish cast upon the highway the lily will grow full of sweet perfume and delight, thus the disciple of the truly enlightened Buddha shines forth by his knowledge among those who are like rubbish, among the people that walk in darkness.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The world does not know that we must all come to an end here;--but those who know it, their quarrels cease at once.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Long is the night to him who is awake; long is a mile to him who is tired; long is life to the foolish who do not know the true law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: "These sons belong to me, and this wealth belongs to me," with such thoughts a fool is tormented. He himself does not belong to himself; how much less sons and wealth?
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If a fool be associated with a wise man even all his life, he will perceive the truth as little as a spoon perceives the taste of soup.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Fools of little understanding have themselves for their greatest enemies, for they do evil deeds which must bear bitter fruits.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: That deed is not well done of which a man must repent, and the reward of which he receives crying and with a tearful face.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As long as the evil deed done does not bear fruit, the fool thinks it is like honey; but when it ripens, then the fool suffers grief.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who lives looking for pleasures only, his senses uncontrolled, immoderate in his food, idle, and weak, Mara (the tempter) will certainly overthrow him, as the wind throws down a weak tree.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let a fool month after month eat his food (like an ascetic) with the tip of a blade of Kusa grass, yet he is not worth the sixteenth particle of those who have well weighed the law.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: An evil deed, like newly-drawn milk, does not turn (suddenly); smouldering, like fire covered by ashes, it follows the fool.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: And when the evil deed, after it has become known, brings sorrow to the fool, then it destroys his bright lot, nay, it cleaves his head.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let the fool wish for a false reputation, for precedence among the Bhikshus, for lordship in the convents, for worship among other people!
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: "May both the layman and he who has left the world think that this is done by me; may they be subject to me in everything which is to be done or is not to be done," thus is the mind of the fool, and his desire and pride increase.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: "One is the road that leads to wealth, another the road that leads to Nirvana;" if the Bhikshu, the disciple of Buddha, has learnt this, he will not yearn for honour, he will strive after separation from the world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If you see an intelligent man who tells you where true treasures are to be found, who shows what is to be avoided, and administers reproofs, follow that wise man; it will be better, not worse, for those who follow him.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Let him admonish, let him teach, let him forbid what is improper!--he will be beloved of the good, by the bad he will be hated.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who lives without looking for pleasures, his senses well controlled, moderate in his food, faithful and strong, him Mara will certainly not overthrow, any more than the wind throws down a rocky mountain.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Good people walk on whatever befall, the good do not prattle, longing for pleasure; whether touched by happiness or sorrow wise people never appear elated or depressed.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: If, whether for his own sake, or for the sake of others, a man wishes neither for a son, nor for wealth, nor for lordship, and if he does not wish for his own success by unfair means, then he is good, wise, and virtuous.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Few are there among men who arrive at the other shore (become Arhats); the other people here run up and down the shore.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: But those who, when the law has been well preached to them, follow the law, will pass across the dominion of death, however difficult to overcome.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Those whose mind is well grounded in the (seven) elements of knowledge, who without clinging to anything, rejoice in freedom from attachment, whose appetites have been conquered, and who are full of light, are free (even) in this world.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He who wishes to put on the yellow dress without having cleansed himself from sin, who disregards temperance and truth, is unworthy of the yellow dress.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: There is no suffering for him who has finished his journey, and abandoned grief, who has freed himself on all sides, and thrown off all fetters.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: They depart with their thoughts well-collected, they are not happy in their abode; like swans who have left their lake, they leave their house and home.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Men who have no riches, who live on recognised food, who have perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), their path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: He whose appetites are stilled, who is not absorbed in enjoyment, who has perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), his path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The gods even envy him whose senses, like horses well broken in by the driver, have been subdued, who is free from pride, and free from appetites.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Such a one who does his duty is tolerant like the earth, like Indra's bolt; he is like a lake without mud; no new births are in store for him.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: The man who is free from credulity, but knows the uncreated, who has cut all ties, removed all temptations, renounced all desires, he is the greatest of men.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: In a hamlet or in a forest, in the deep water or on the dry land, wherever venerable persons (Arhanta) dwell, that place is delightful.
quotes.author: The Buddha

quotes.text: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.
quotes.author: The Buddha
